summary: Dependency-confusion probe exfiltrates host and CI metadata to Burp Collaborator on install
details: The package ships beacon.js and wires it to all four npm lifecycle hooks (preinstall, install, postinstall, prepare), so `npm install @eforms/forms-api` runs it unconditionally. beacon.js collects host identifiers (os.hostname(), os.userInfo(), process.cwd(), platform, Node version) and a selected set of environment variables including CI and npm configuration (e.g. npm_config_registry), serializes them to JSON, base64-encodes the payload and truncates to 900 characters. It then exfiltrates the payload over two channels to the hardcoded Burp Collaborator (OAST) host 2z237udr1jxdaiw54xzmzfb7nytohszuplipn34fm4.oastify.com: as a DNS label via dns.lookup() and as a query string via https.get(). The dual DNS+HTTPS delivery is designed to bypass egress filtering. The `@eforms/*` scope and `forms-api` name are consistent with a dependency-confusion probe targeting an internal package of the same name. The 'research canary' framing in the source does not change the behavior: the beacon fires on any installer and sends installer-identifying data to an attacker-controlled collector.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
